local_calendar.t: On November 3, 2026 Washington elects county officers (assessor, auditor, clerk, coroner, prosecuting attorney, sheriff, treasurer, and commissioner or council seats), district court judges and public utility district commissioners, and fills 4 unexpired superior court terms; a county office carries party preferences unless the county's charter makes it nonpartisan. Cities, towns, school districts and most other districts (fire, port, hospital, water, park) elect their officers in November of odd-numbered years, next in 2027, so only a few of their seats are on this ballot: 2 city council seats, 6 port and fire district seats and the municipal court judges of Seattle and Tacoma. Conservation districts hold their elections at times set by their own law, and a county charter may put county elections in odd-numbered years.
local_calendar.s: Revised Code of Washington 29A.04.321 and 29A.04.330 (when state, county, city and district elections are held), 29A.04.110 (partisan offices), 36.16.030 (elective county officers), 3.34.050 (district judges) and 35.20.150 (Seattle's municipal judges); the Secretary of State's GENERAL 2026 Candidate List for what is on this ballot

local_coverage.t: Loaded: every contest for a county, city or district office with a candidate on the Secretary of State's GENERAL 2026 Candidate List, read county by county for all 39 counties: 282 contests for county offices, 133 for superior, district and municipal court judges (shown with the judges), 31 for public utility district commissioners and 8 for city council, port and fire district seats, 624 candidates in all. Not loaded: ballot measures, levies and other questions, which the candidate list does not carry; write-in candidates; any office nobody filed for; and the local primaries of August 4. A district is named in the list's own words with the county or counties whose lists carry it, because the list gives no district numbers.
local_coverage.s: Washington Secretary of State, GENERAL 2026 Candidate List

gaps.w: write-in candidates for county and local offices
gaps.r: The Secretary of State's candidate list names only the candidates printed on the ballot. A write-in candidate declares with the county auditor and is not on this list.
The Secretary of State's list is a list of candidates, so an office that nobody filed for does not appear on it. The county auditor's sample ballot is the authority for such an office.
